content: 1. Fexinidazole: Avoid or consider alternative drugs. Fexinidazole inhibits CYP3A4, and coadministration may increase the risk of adverse effects associated with CYP3A4 substrates. Close monitoring is recommended. 2. Netupitant/Palonosetron and Finererone: Netupitant/palonosetron increases the levels or effects of finererone by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Monitor serum potassium levels during initiation and dosage adjustments of either finererone or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. Adjust finererone dosage as needed. 3. Netupitant/Palonosetron and Flibanserin: Coadministration is contraindicated. Netupitant/palonosetron increases the levels or effects of flibanserin by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Severe hypotension or syncope may occur. Avoid combining flibanserin with moderate or strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 4. Netupitant/Palonosetron and Fluoxetine: Both drugs increase each other's toxicity through serotonin level modulation. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 5. Netupitant/Palonosetron and Fluvoxamine: Fluvoxamine increases the toxicity of netupitant/palonosetron by affecting serotonin levels. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 6. Fosamprenavir: Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of netupitant/palonosetron by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. No dosage adjustment is required for netupitant. 7. Fosphenytoin: Fosphenytoin decreases the levels or effects of netupitant/palonosetron by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Avoid netupitant in patients chronically using strong CYP3A4 inducers. 8. Netupitant/Palonosetron and Frovatriptan: Both drugs increase each other's toxicity through serotonin level modulation. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 9. Netupitant/Palonosetron and Gepirone: Netupitant/palonosetron increases the levels or effects of gepirone by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the gepirone dose by 50% when used with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. Monitor closely. 10. Grapefruit: Grapefruit increases the levels or effects of netupitant/palonosetron by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. No dosage adjustment is required for netupitant. 11. Netupitant/Palonosetron and Guanfacine: Netupitant/palonosetron increases the levels or effects of guanfacine by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors significantly increase guanfacine plasma concentrations. For extended-release guanfacine, reduce the dose to half if coadministered. No specific recommendations are available for immediate-release guanfacine. 12. Netupitant/Palonosetron and Ibrutinib: Netupitant/palonosetron increases the levels or effects of ibrutinib by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the ibrutinib dose to 280 mg daily (for B-cell malignancies) or 420 mg daily (for graft-versus-host disease) when coadministered with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. Resume the previous dose after discontinuation of the CYP3A4 inhibitor. 13. Idelalisib: Idelalisib increases the levels or effects of netupitant/palonosetron by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. No dosage adjustment is required for netupitant. 14. Ifosfamide: Netupitant/palonosetron decreases the effects of ifosfamide by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 15. Imatinib: Imatinib increases the levels or effects of netupitant/palonosetron by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. No dosage adjustment is required for netupitant. 16. Netupitant/Palonosetron and Imipramine: Both drugs increase each other's toxicity through serotonin level modulation. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 17. Indinavir: Indinavir increases the levels or effects of netupitant/palonosetron by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. No dosage adjustment is required for netupitant. 18. Netupitant/Palonosetron and Infigratinib: Netupitant/palonosetron increases the levels or effects of infigratinib by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 19. Irinotecan: Netupitant/palonosetron increases the levels or effects of irinotecan by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 20. Isavuconazonium Sulfate: Netupitant/palonosetron increases the levels or effects of isavuconazonium sulfate by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 21. Netupitant/Palonosetron and Isocarboxazid: Both drugs increase each other's toxicity through serotonin level modulation. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 22. Isoniazid: Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of netupitant/palonosetron by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. No dosage adjustment is required for netupitant. 23. Istradefylline: Istradefylline increases the levels or effects of netupitant/palonosetron by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Consider dose reduction of sensitive CYP3A4 substrates. Monitor closely. 24. Itraconazole: Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of netupitant/palonosetron by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. No dosage adjustment is required for netupitant. 25. Netupitant/Palonosetron and Ivabradine: Netupitant/palonosetron increases the levels or effects of ivabradine by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Avoid coadministration of ivabradine with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 26. Ivacaftor: Netupitant/palonosetron increases the levels or effects of ivacaftor by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the ivacaftor dose if coadministered with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. Refer to specific ivacaftor-containing product guidelines for precise dosage adjustments. 27. Ivosidenib: Netupitant/palonosetron increases the levels or effects of ivosidenib by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Coadministration with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase ivosidenib plasma concentrations, raising the risk of QTc prolongation. 28. Ketoconazole: Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of netupitant/palonosetron by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. No dosage adjustment is required for netupitant. 29. Netupitant/Palonosetron and Lemborexant: Netupitant/palonosetron increases the levels or effects of lemborexant by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Avoid coadministration of lemborexant with moderate or strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 30. Levomilnacipran: Both drugs increase each other's toxicity through serotonin level modulation. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 31. Lonafarnib: Netupitant/palonosetron increases the levels or effects of lonafarnib by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Coadministration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors is contraindicated. 32. Lopinavir: Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of netupitant/palonosetron by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. No dosage adjustment is required for netupitant. 33. Lorlatinib: Lorlatinib decreases the levels or effects of netupitant/palonosetron by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 34. Lurbinectedin: Netupitant/palonosetron increases the levels or effects of lurbinectedin by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 35. Mavacamten: Netupitant/palonosetron increases the levels or effects of mavacamten by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Initiation of moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors may require a reduced mavacamten dose. Monitor closely. 36. Mavorixafor: Netupitant/palonosetron increases the levels or effects of mavorixafor by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor for adverse effects and reduce the mavorixafor dose if necessary. 37. Midazolam (Intranasal): Netupitant/palonosetron increases the levels or effects of intranasal midazolam by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Coadministration with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors may prolong sedation. 38. Milnacipran: Both drugs increase each other's toxicity through serotonin level modulation. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 39. Mitotane: Mitotane decreases the levels or effects of netupitant/palonosetron by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Avoid netupitant in patients chronically using strong CYP3A4 inducers. 40. Nafcillin: Nafcillin decreases the levels or effects of netupitant/palonosetron by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Avoid netupitant in patients chronically using strong CYP3A4 inducers. 41. Naldemedine: Netupitant/palonosetron increases the levels of naldemedine by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor for potential adverse effects. 42. Neratinib: Netupitant/palonosetron increases the levels or effects of neratinib by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Avoid coadministration of neratinib with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 43. Nevirapine: Nevirapine decreases the levels or effects of netupitant/palonosetron by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Avoid netupitant in patients chronically using strong CYP3A4 inducers. 44. Nicardipine: Nicardipine increases the levels or effects of netupitant/palonosetron by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. No dosage adjustment is required for netupitant. 45. Nirogacestat: Netupitant/palonosetron increases the levels or effects of nirogacestat by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 46. Norgestrel: Netupitant/palonosetron increases the levels or effects of norgestrel by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor for adverse effects. 47. Nortriptyline: Both drugs increase each other's toxicity through serotonin level modulation. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 48. Olaparib: Netupitant/palonosetron increases the levels or effects of olaparib by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. If coadministration with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors cannot be avoided, reduce the olaparib dose to 200 mg (capsule) or 150 mg (tablet) twice daily. Do not substitute tablets with capsules.
